cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a hand-woven strip-cloth tobe/boubou gown with indigo and pale purple stripes and embroidered breast panel, a garment type worn across the wider West African region including Wolof communities of Senegal; the craft and form are plausible for the claimed culture.

physical.title: gown; tobe
physical.summary: Gown (tobe, boubou, agbada): assembled from 76 narrow strips of hand-spun cotton, hand-woven and sewn together by hand along the selvedges. The body is flared by folding the strips towards the top; the strips of the sleeves are not folded but are wider at the top than the bottom. The strips are primarily of indigo-dyed thread, and all have the same pattern, a variant of ‘saki’ or ‘etu’, with threads of pale purple cotton (also hand-spun, and possibly of alaari silk) run regularly along both warp and weft. In this case, however, two shades of indigo are used, and there is a wider band of white threads running along the centre of each strip. Both the neck opening and the vestigial non-functional pockets are edged with embroidered lines of white cotton; there are also twelve knot patterns in chain stitch on the front.
